To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the ob/ob mouse has a lower resting oxygen consumption than the +/+ mouse at every ambient temperature tested; 2) the ob/ ob mouse has a lower core temperature than the +/+ or ob/+ mouse at every temperature tested; 3) the +/+ mouse has a significantly higher resting oxygen consumption than either the ob/ob or ob/+ mouse; and 4) the +/+ and ob/+ mice have similar core temperatures at each ambient temperature.

the development of an animal model for obesity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ob/ob mouse is a model for the study of the pathophysiology of human obesity.
the obese mice are less metabolically active than the thin animals and that these differences are evident prior to the phenotypical expression of obesity.
